milestone: M56 Arbitrary Repository Coding Golden Journey

strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: headless.continue_once can now consume the objective apply continuation checkpoint, recompute the current target SHA-256 after mutation, and route deterministically to completion acceptance or verification recovery without caller-side file inspection.
The runtime verifies the M56.4 replace_file apply evidence before trusting the mutation result, preserving Rust ownership of workspace state transitions.
The Golden Journey gains an explicit replay-safe route between objective apply and accepted completion or recovery, rather than falling back to generic progress inspection.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development with direct support for controlled_workspace_tools, agent_loop, runtime_permission_enforcement, and persistent_structured_ledger.
answers.new_capability: A headless caller can provide objective_apply_verification_target to headless.continue_once and have Rust validate prior objective apply provenance, recompute current target SHA-256, checkpoint the verification, and route to accept_objective_completion or start_verification_recovery.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: M56.4 can perform the replace_file mutation but only routed to progress inspection; it did not prove that the current workspace target still matches the post-write hash or choose the next Golden Journey branch from bounded evidence.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: The autonomous Golden Journey would mutate a file but still require caller-side inspection to decide whether the objective is safe to complete or recovery should begin.
answers.non_duplicative: Distinct from M56.2 candidate binding, M56.3 authorization/preflight, and M56.4 objective apply because this phase verifies the already-applied target and chooses the next route from current workspace state.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The phase extends existing headless.continue_once params and result routing; it adds no JSON-RPC method.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. It adds no report, digest, history, verdict, readiness, inspection, preview, or dashboard surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Rust now validates objective apply checkpoint evidence, hashes the current target file, records bounded verification checkpoint/event evidence, and routes verified matches to completion acceptance or mismatches to recovery.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: The scheduled controller can continue after a workspace mutation without manually reading file content, using replay-safe bounded verification evidence to choose the next action.
answers.milestone_progress: This closes the post-apply verification gap in M56 and enables a following acceptance phase to complete the arbitrary repository coding Golden Journey.

exit_criteria: headless.continue_once accepts a bounded objective_apply_verification_target for verify_objective_apply_explicitly routes

Rust validates the M56.4 objective apply checkpoint identity, decision id, journey/session/drive/task/run/proposal/apply ids, operation/status labels, authorization consumption, apply fingerprint, path fingerprint, and expected post-write SHA-256
Rust recomputes the current target file SHA-256 through workspace-relative apply target resolution without exposing raw file content
Matching current hash writes a bounded verification checkpoint and returns next_route.kind = accept_objective_completion_explicitly with next_action = accept_objective_completion
Mismatched current hash writes bounded mismatch evidence and returns next_route.kind = start_verification_recovery_explicitly with next_action = start_verification_recovery
Exact replay returns the same bounded route/checkpoint evidence without duplicating ledger events or reading raw caller-owned content into responses

Ledger/checkpoint/RPC payloads exclude raw prompts, provider responses, file content, diffs, stdout/stderr, commands, environment, raw requests, raw ledger payloads, absolute/canonical paths, secrets, and raw tokens
behavior_evidence: Rust behavior test headless_continue_applies_objective_proposal_after_authorization_preflight_and_replays covers objective apply verification success, replay, mismatch routing, bounded checkpointing, and no raw content ledger exposure
cargo check --workspace validates protocol/runtime/store integration for objective apply verification target and checkpoint types
VSIX protocol tests accept bounded objective apply verification params and reject malformed or raw-data-bearing payloads

safety_boundary: uses existing M56.4 objective apply checkpoint evidence
requires explicit objective apply verification authorization
reads target bytes only to compute SHA-256 and never returns or persists raw file content
stores bounded hashes, identifiers, route, status, and sequence metadata only
non_goals: no shell, git, network, provider, service, scheduler, or daemon execution
rejected_alternatives: caller-side file inspection after M56.4 apply
routing directly from apply to accepted completion without recomputing current target hash
adding a verification report or preview endpoint
persisting raw file content, diffs, raw requests, commands, or environment in verification evidence
technical_debt: A following phase must add the explicit accepted-completion route before the Golden Journey can terminally close.
Runtime lib.rs remains large and should be split only by a later behavior-preserving MOVE-only refactor.
next_capability_rationale: M56.6 should consume the accepted objective completion route and record terminal Golden Journey completion from bounded verification evidence.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M56.5 updates current and archived phase-value manifests for the objective apply verification route. Review must confirm guard enforcement is not weakened and no wrapper/report/readiness surface was added.
